title: Basic Types
description: Learn TypeScript's primitive and built-in types.

data.text: TypeScript provides several basic types that form the foundation of type annotations. Understanding these primitives is essential before moving to more complex types.

terms.definition: Numeric values, both integers and floats
Large integers beyond safe integer limit

data.title: Primitives
Arrays

cards.title: any
cards.description: Opts out of type checking entirely. Avoid unless absolutely necessary.

cards.title: unknown
cards.description: Safer alternative to any. Requires type checking before use.

cards.title: never
cards.description: Represents values that never occur. Used for functions that always throw.

data.title: Special Types

data.text: TypeScript can infer types automatically, so you don't always need explicit annotations.

data.title: Inference
Prefer Inference
data.text: Let TypeScript infer types when possible. Add explicit annotations only when necessary for clarity or when inference fails.

items.question: Should I always write type annotations?
items.answer: No. TypeScript infers types in most cases. Add annotations when the type isn't obvious or when you need a specific type like a union.

items.question: When should I use 'any'?
items.answer: Rarely. Only when migrating legacy code or dealing with untyped third-party libraries. Always prefer 'unknown' when you can.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Tuples: fixed-length arrays with specific types
data.takeaway: Basic types are the building blocks of TypeScript.
